## 2. Requirements and quality attributes

| ID | Design requirement | Release evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SD01 | Private operations plus optional marketplace; distinguish business, customer, patient and app user | Unlisted business completes direct service/sale; private data never appears in public discovery |
| SD02 | Business/branch/assignment and patient-purpose authorization | Negative list/detail/write/export/file tests for two businesses and revoked staff |
| SD03 | One stock authority across app, counter and procedure consumption | Last-unit race, batch-correct returns, transfer/wastage reconciliation |
| SD04 | Shared appointment capacity with payment compensation | Concurrent holds, expiry/capture race and safe cancellation |
| SD05 | Common lab lifecycle for API and panel; signed/versioned reports | Duplicate/reordered provider events, reviewer roles and corrected-report access |
| SD06 | Separate financial documents and immutable money effects | Capture/refund/cash/credit/commission/payout reconciliations |
| SD07 | Patient identity, consent, clinical history and care continuity | No-phone/caregiver flow, reviewed duplicate mapping, amendment and follow-up ownership |
| SD08 | Durable asynchronous work and bounded provider dependencies | Crash/replay/timeout tests and visible recovery queues |
| SD09 | 100 aggregate incoming HTTP RPS on useful mixed work | Per-class latency/error gates plus stock/slot/money/access integrity |
| SD10 | Migration, restore, observability and upgrade ownership | Rehearsed cutover/rollback and restore with reconciled documents/events |

Proposed performance gates remain those in [PERFORMANCE_PLAN.md](PERFORMANCE_PLAN.md): list/simple reads p95 <=500 ms; local transactional commands p95 <=1,000 ms; authenticated durable webhook acknowledgement p95 <=300 ms; unexpected failures <0.1%; zero integrity violations. Provider completion has a separate SLO. Proposed recovery objectives are RPO <=15 minutes and RTO <=2 hours, subject to budget/operations approval; they are not current guarantees.

## 5. Business tenancy, patient identity and access

Initial storage: shared Mongo database/collections, with mandatory `organizationId` on private business records and `branchId`/department/store where relevant. Do not add a meaningless tenant field to global reference data or mistake a global patient identity for shared clinical access. Clinical artifacts belong to their responsible organization plus explicit authorized care relationships.

Build staff request context from verified identity and active membership: `actorId`, actor kind, organization, allowed branches, role capabilities, assignments and purpose. A path/body/header organization is a requested scope; the server verifies membership before using it. Patient/caregiver principals instead carry verified patient relationships and purpose, without requiring business membership; the service resolves the target record's business and intersects patient rights with release/sharing policy. A dual-role user chooses the active purpose, never a union of patient and staff privileges. Deny by default. Scope lists, counts, detail, mutations, aggregates, exports, document grants and background jobs. Administrative cross-business access is a separate audited capability with reason and MFA; support has no routine full-record access. [OWASP object-level authorization](https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization/).

**Repository enforcement point.** Business-owned collections are accessible through a typed scoped repository/query gateway requiring verified `BusinessScope` (organization, permitted branches and actor/purpose). Methods cover ID reads, lists/counts, insert/upsert, update/delete, bulk and aggregation. They compose caller criteria with restrictive scope, reject caller-supplied ownership changes and deny an empty/invalid scope. Joins/lookups must scope each private collection and verify cross-record ownership; an arbitrary FilterQuery alone is not a security contract.

CI import/architecture rules prohibit direct business-model access outside approved scoped adapters and the explicit audited admin adapter. Runtime guards fail closed on missing scope and emit a redacted security event; merely alerting after an unscoped query is insufficient. Global reference collections are enumerated separately. The existing unscoped `BaseRepository` remains a legacy implementation until migrated: new business modules cannot use it directly, while M0 fixes existing caller ownership and migration wrappers before M1 extends the shared model. Two-business/branch fixtures exercise real list/detail/count/aggregate/export/file/jobs and write paths; static lint cannot prove arbitrary query correctness by itself.

| Actor | Normal access | Additional condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patient/caregiver | Verified own/represented care and bills | Explicit account-to-patient relationship; shared phone is insufficient |
| Reception/cashier | Branch registration, queue, permitted tariffs and receipts | No clinical signoff, unrestricted exports or refund override |
| Doctor | Assigned encounters/history needed for care, prescriptions and reviews | Author/finalization permissions and current sharing policy |
| Lab technician/signatory | Assigned orders/specimens; signatory approves reports | Technician cannot self-promote or release outside authorized scope |
| Pharmacy/store staff | Assigned store operations and minimum prescription context | Pharmacist release/stock adjustments require designated capabilities |
| Independent vendor | Assigned commercial/service records and permitted statements | No whole patient chart or another business's private prices |
| Integration worker | Narrow command/business scope | Persist initiator; re-evaluate revocable permissions for sensitive delayed actions |

Minimal patient identity may be global, but search results are limited to authorized local relationships or a verified patient-led linking flow. Do not expose cross-business identity existence through autocomplete. Clinical services need `patientId`; wholesale buyers/nonclinical customers can be businesses without patient identity. Payer and patient are separate references.

Consent records capture purpose, scope, version, representative, method/language, provenance and effective/withdrawal times. Authorization evaluates current restrictions, assignment and approved legal basis; a blanket consent boolean or marketplace listing is insufficient. Withdrawal blocks future optional sharing/sends while historical record retention follows approved policy. Emergency access, minor/guardian rules, retention/legal holds and cross-business sharing require clinical/privacy signoff before enabling those paths.

CASL is a candidate policy library, not a tenancy guarantee. Revocation updates membership version; sensitive commands check current membership rather than trusting long-lived token roles. Keep existing authentication behind a strengthened interface; no fallback production JWT secret, fixed OTP bypass or unrestricted diagnostic/admin endpoints. Public listing off preserves accepted obligations and private workspace access.

## 7. Transactions, concurrency and idempotency

Mongo is the initial authoritative transactional store. Multi-document transactions require the supported replica-set/sharded deployment and configured durability; existing inventory already depends on sessions. Use short transactions with appropriate majority durability/read concerns verified against the selected server/driver. Bound retry of transient/unknown-commit outcomes and consult the command result before replaying effects. [MongoDB transactions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions/).

Every financial/stock/capacity-changing command needs a scoped idempotency key and normalized request hash. In one transaction, establish the unique command record, check actor/resource version and expected state, change owned records, append audit/effects and outbox, and persist the command result/reference. Concurrent duplicate keys resolve to the committed original result; a different body returns 409. Never leave a permanently unowned processing key: use transaction atomicity or a recoverable lease. Authentication/authorization precede returning any stored response.

| Command | Local atomic boundary | External work / compensation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Place pharmacy order | Order + explicit lot reservation + effect/audit/outbox + command result | Create gateway intent after commit; failure releases through a guarded command |
| Counter cash dispense | Approved prescription/price + order/invoice + receipt/journal + stock movement, if bounded | No gateway call; print/send after commit. Large bulk sale uses bounded drafts before final commit |
| Appointment hold | Conditional capacity increment + hold/appointment + outbox/result | Payment intent afterward; expiry/cancellation releases once |
| Apply verified collection | Unique capture effect + receipt/journal + allowed local booking/order transition | External fulfilment queued; failure enters recovery/refund policy |
| Finalize report | Expected draft version/signatory + release pointer + audit + review task/outbox | Notifications/webhooks after commit, only for approved recipients |
| Receive purchase/transfer | Remaining receivable check + lot balance + immutable movement + receipt state | Supplier payment/account export separately owned |
| Wallet reserve/capture/release | Guard selected account/pocket available funds and hold version; update posted/held counters, hold/movement, booking state and outbox/result together | External call facts are reconciled before expiry/capture; release and capture are mutually exclusive for the same amount |
| Refund completion | Confirmed provider result + unique refund effect/journal + refund state | Stock return and credit note remain explicit linked commands |

**M0 wallet mutation boundary (AR-14).** Every live customer-wallet debit/credit/refund uses one owned application operation and Mongo session: establish the unique economic effect key, conditionally update the authoritative balance with `$inc` (debit predicate requires available funds: posted minus held >= debit, within the selected currency/account and permitted purpose), insert the movement/transaction row, update dependent local booking/payment state and append outbox/result atomically. Duplicate effect keys return the committed original result; a crash rolls back both balance and movement. Partial wallet funding is selected under that transaction and snapshotted into the payment intent; a retry cannot deduct again or silently change a live gateway amount. [MongoDB atomic updates](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/write-operations-atomicity/).

Target wallet commands include reserve, capture and release as explicit idempotent operations. Authoritative posted/held counters share a guarded account/pocket document; available = posted - held and posted >= held >= 0. Reserving raises held only when available covers the amount; capture reduces posted and held once; release reduces held once. Ordinary debit/transfer and competing app/phone holds check that same available counter, not a snapshot sum of hold rows. Preserve any proven active holds in migration. Legacy held=0 is allowed only after confirming none exist; the new F14 hold workflow is not a new M0 dependency, but cannot launch until all affected debit paths enforce this contract.

M0 compatibility preserves an explicit balance-unit/currency contract; never increment a legacy rupee balance with unlabelled paise or silently change an existing gateway split. The normalized minor-unit cutover follows the reviewed pre-M2 migration. Replace the seven inspected read/insert/absolute-balance-update paths in bookings, externalBookings, payment recharge/refund and wallet services. The existing atomic credit and pharmacy-wallet guarded-debit helpers are useful primitives, but `$inc` alone does not atomically bind the ledger or suppress duplicates. Remove absolute read-modify-set balance mutations from normal flows; controlled initial creation and reviewed opening-balance cutover are separate initialization operations. Cover every reference type, not only the existing pharmacy-order refund partial index. Use operation identity for legitimate partial refunds and enforce the remaining refundable amount; do not wrongly deduplicate all partial refunds into one booking-wide key.

F13 verifies the wallet-effect uniqueness manifest and existing pharmacy+medicine unique index before affected mutations are enabled. Resolve duplicate/missing legacy evidence explicitly; never delete conflicting financial history to make an index build succeed. Mandatory tests: two wallet-funded bookings against funds for one; duplicate refunds; legitimate distinct partial refunds; crash between balance and movement writes; missing-index refusal. These are unexecuted release gates.

Use compare-and-set on state/version and conditional quantity/capacity predicates; application read-then-write checks alone are insufficient. If several FEFO lots are needed, deterministic selection and guarded decrements occur within the same bounded transaction. On contention retry selection; reject shortages without partial allocation. Available units = eligible on-hand minus reserved, excluding quarantined/expired stock.

Holds/reservations have explicit expiresAt, active/reconciling/capture-pending/consumed/released state and allocation records. Expiry and confirm race through guarded versions; only one wins. An open payment requires the bounded gateway-reconciliation protocol in section 9 before final release; the network call occurs outside the transaction while a fenced reconciling claim protects capacity. Commands reject an expired hold unless that explicit payment decision preserves it; delayed cleanup alone never extends a hold. Never delete live reservation/hold documents with TTL: capacity/stock release and audit must commit first. TTL is only later cleanup under retention policy; MongoDB does not promise immediate expiry deletion. [TTL behavior](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-ttl/).

### 8.1 Pharmacy and connected counter

Order: draft -> reserved -> accepted -> dispensing -> fulfilled; cancellation/expiry/partial fulfilment are explicit branches. Prescription verification/rejection and payment status are separate gates. Postpaid/cash policy may permit dispensing before a collection only for an authorized business configuration; it creates receivable, not a fictitious paid receipt.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Counter or app
  participant A as API PaymentIntentCoordinator
  participant D as Mongo transaction
  participant W as Recovery worker
  participant G as Payment gateway
  C->>A: Place order with idempotency key
  A->>D: Commit price, order, FEFO hold and creating payment intent
  D-->>A: Durable business and receipt references
  A->>G: Create gateway order outside transaction
  G-->>A: External reference or unknown timeout
  A->>D: Persist reference or recoverable unknown
  A-->>C: Checkout details or explicit processing result
  G->>A: Authenticated payment event
  A->>D: Durable inbox; captured fact required for collection
  W->>D: Apply money and guarded hold/recovery decision once
  C->>A: Authorized dispense command
  A->>D: Check prescription/payment policy and consume held lots
```

Retail/wholesale is price entitlement, not a duplicate stock pool. Snapshot approved buyer eligibility, tariff/rule version, minimum quantities, tax and UOM; do not trust client-calculated totals. An authorized counter price override is supported: staff capability, actor, reason, original/approved unit price, limit/approval policy and timestamp are recorded; the server recomputes totals/tax and snapshots the override. Existing unrestricted input is a gap to harden, not a requirement to remove all overrides. Partial fulfilment adjusts charge/refund and quantities explicitly. Customer returns reference original lines/lots and quantities already returned; inspect and quarantine where required before making stock saleable. Expired/recalled stock cannot re-enter usable inventory through a generic increment helper. Expiry is evaluated using the store's configured local date and approved manufacturer expiry precision/cutoff, not UTC `today`. The existing UTC YYYYMMDD comparison can retain stock after the intended local cutoff (up to 5h30 for Asia/Kolkata under end-of-local-day policy); test the boundary, month/date precision and every reserve/consume/release/list path. Unknown expiry is quarantined/reviewed, never fabricated.

Supplies use the same purchasing/location/movement principles but different item/service rules. A lab procedure consumes actual approved reagents once using a service-use key; record waste/overrides and reversals. A BOM is a proposal until staff confirms use. Included consumables do not produce a second customer charge. Transfers move source -> in-transit -> destination; destination rejects/shortfalls remain visible. Stock counts create authorized variances, not rewritten movement history.

**AR-27 quality transitions.** Receipt, count, adjustment, import, cancel, release and return preserve recalled, quarantined, expired or other quality holds regardless of positive quantity. Availability/depletion and quality approval are separate decisions. Only a separately authorized, version-checked quality-release command with evidence may change a releasable hold; manufacturer expiry/recall policy cannot be bypassed by quantity authorization. Use the current representation safely in M0; define any two-axis schema and historical mapping before M3.

**AR-32 lot price and quote contract.** For applicable medicines/packaged goods, validate the tax-inclusive allocated-unit charge against the applicable label/lot MRP and any lower verified current price-list/controlled limit, using exact pack-to-selling-unit conversion. Never add tax twice or use the latest item's display price as every FEFO lot's authority. Discounts, slabs and overrides cannot defeat that ceiling. Missing/ambiguous lot price/unit evidence requires approved review or safe refusal, not an invented unlimited cap. Preserve original sold terms on returns. Repricing a customer-originated placed order needs a new quote version and customer confirmation; an authorized counter override retains actor/reason/limits and is not general permission to rewrite a paid order. Finance/pharmacist/legal owners approve current applicability, source updates and units before the affected pricing release; this is not a legal certification. The Ministry describes inclusive MRP and the lower label/current-price-list constraint; later amendments and SKU/jurisdiction applicability still need owner review. [Official medicine pricing explanation](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1983964&lang=2&reg=3).

### 8.3 API and panel laboratories

Lab order: requested -> accepted -> collection scheduled/collected -> received -> processing -> verified -> released. Rejection, recollection, cancellation and amendment are explicit branches; map provider states, retaining original evidence. Remote labs may not expose every sample stage: mark unknown/provider-reported rather than inventing it.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Jansetu order API
  participant D as Mongo and durable events
  participant L as Lab API adapter or lab panel
  participant R as Authorized report reviewer
  participant C as Clinician and patient access
  A->>D: Order + lab assignment + fulfilment mode
  D->>L: Scoped command or assigned worklist
  L->>A: Provider event or panel sample/report command
  A->>D: Authenticate, deduplicate, map and validate state
  R->>A: Approve and release specific report version
  A->>D: Release + private metadata + review task + outbox
  D-->>C: Authorized report-ready event and review work
```

Fulfilment mode is snapshotted per assignment, not inferred from whether a lab later adds an API. Handing an order between modes requires an authorized handover, paused old writer, version increment, reconciled provider order and clear report provenance. Do not create a duplicate commercial order or let both modes finalize the same report. An API-delivered report still needs an established lab approval contract; do not blindly mark any uploaded PDF clinically verified. Use separate axes: acquisition `received`; completeness `preliminary|final|unknown`; approval/publication `draft|verified|released|rejected|superseded`. An amendment creates a new version linked by `amendsVersionId`, rather than modifying final bytes. A permitted preliminary release is conspicuously labelled with provider provenance/pending scope and does not imply all tests are final. Lab/clinical/privacy owners decide preliminary release and correction-notice policy before the pilot.

Every semantically new fetch/upload uses an immutable organization/order/version-scoped object key plus content hash and a version manifest. A hash is not a public lookup key or authorization. Duplicate callbacks with identical bytes, stage and provenance record delivery evidence without creating another clinical version; changed completeness/status can create a new version even with identical bytes. Release conditionally moves the current pointer and reopens/links clinician review; past review remains tied to its exact version. Corrections notify only currently permitted recipients through approved care/legal-basis rules, with ordering-clinician escalation where allowed; never silently add recipients after consent withdrawal. M0 stops stable-name overwrite and public cache use; legacy files retain `versionHistory: unknown` when prior bytes cannot be recovered.

**AR-35 existing provider fulfilment recovery.** Persist one scoped fulfilment intent/result for the local obligation and assigned provider before create. Concurrent client verification, worker and webhook paths cannot independently place the same provider order. Use provider-supported idempotency/reference lookup and account/integration-scoped external IDs; where capability is absent, retain pending/manual reconciliation rather than blind retry. Treat network reset, timeout and ambiguous 5xx as unknown until evidence resolves them. Preserve existing confirmation-pending behavior already present in some paths; do not claim that every timeout currently refunds. A local timer or cancellation request does not prove provider failure/cancellation or justify a completed refund. Refund obligations, actual returns and provider cancellation are distinct, with the shared captured-source budget. Authorized manual resolution requires reason/evidence and cannot bypass that budget. M0 covers the existing lab-payment fulfilment/recovery implementation; API-to-panel expansion remains M4. The owner confirmed pre-launch with no real patients/payments on 9 November 2026; existing code paths do not establish live deployment.

## 15. Failure handling and observability

| Failure / race | Required behavior | Detection / recovery owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Client times out after local commit | Same command key retrieves original authorized result | API/command metrics; backend |
| Capture after hold expiry | Preserve collection; controlled reallocation or refund/recovery | Payment reconciliation and oldest pending-compensation alert; finance/backend |
| Worker crashes after external effect | Replay original identity, lookup external result, avoid duplicate mutation | Lease expiry, delivery attempts and unknown-outcome worklist; integrations |
| Duplicate/stale lab events | Dedupe and preserve report version/state; reconcile gaps | Provider mapping/version metrics; lab operations |
| API and panel both try to act | Expected assignment mode/version fences old writer | Conflict audit and authorized handover; lab lead |
| DB unavailable/unknown commit | No false success; bounded retry/idempotent lookup; preserve external evidence | DB/pool/readiness alerts; DevOps/backend |
| Report/storage/scanner unavailable | Pending artifact, no public fallback or unverified release | Validation/backlog/link checks; documents/lab lead |
| External ERP/LIS unavailable | Pending operation or unavailable capability; no competing native stock writer | Adapter health/reconciliation; facility operations |
| Subscription delinquency | Apply agreed entitlements/grace; preserve data/export/urgent-care continuity under policy | Billing/support worklist; product/operations |
| Credential/revoked-staff event | Rotate/revoke, block sensitive access, audit scope and reissue integrations | Security alerts and incident runbook; security/DevOps |

Logs use request/correlation/operation/event/resource IDs and safe status codes; redact tokens, identifiers beyond need, medical content and raw signatures. Metrics use bounded cardinality rather than patient IDs. Clinical access and privileged changes have protected audit records with actor, purpose, scope, before/after references and outcome; regular business users cannot edit them. Retention and access are separate from application debug logs.

Initial alert proposals: urgent if capture/refund discrepancies appear, unauthorized access occurs, accepted writes cannot reconcile or durable acceptance fails; warn if normal-task p95 age exceeds 30 seconds or backlog grows across successive windows. Clinical urgent-result escalation deadlines are set by the clinical team, not the normal queue SLO. Dashboards separate local API latency, provider completion, money recovery, sample/report turnaround, restore status and store/capacity reconciliation. Each alert/runbook has an accountable human role and replay/correction steps.

Backups encrypt database and object versions with independently protected keys. Restore into an isolated environment and reconcile patient mappings, report hashes, invoice/journal/stock totals, in-flight holds and pending events. After restore, re-pull gateway payment/order/refund and lab-provider facts across an overlapping recovery window from the restore point, compare existing external IDs and captured versions, and queue mismatches without duplicate effects. Source systems may contain newer captures/reports than the backup. Backup success alone does not prove RPO/RTO. Export supports authorized business continuity without exposing another business or silently losing amendments/financial references.

### 15.1 Restore admission and authority freshness (AR-29)

Keep sensitive access, optional sends and irreversible mutations closed while restoring. Advance a recovery generation in a protected control plane outside the restored rollback domain and require all API/worker instances to observe it before admission. Invalidate pre-restore sessions/access grants and all outstanding OTP/setup/reset challenges; do not restore usable consumed challenges. A new token minted after restore is not proof that restored membership, consent, caregiver, contact or credential data is current. Recover post-backup revocation/consumption evidence from an independently recoverable journal or require approved independent re-verification before issuing fresh authority. If freshness cannot be established, keep that subject/scope blocked with an accountable assisted route. Resume sensitive deliveries only after current recipient/purpose/authority is established; regenerated jobs do not inherit stale grants. Select the concrete control-plane/evidence mechanism and failure policy before restore acceptance; no additional microservice or external product is chosen here.

### 15.2 Recoverability of irreversible effects (AR-30)

# Network admission rule contract

**10 November 2026. Amended after pre-review, containment review and Standards review.** Branch `m0/foundation-network-admission`, base `9ea963f`. Internal Claude reviews, each returned to the author for changes:

## 3. Admission rule

Bootstrap always attempts to capture the `APP-NET-DIAG-1` record. Each of the following throws without writing a record:
- port or `runId` validation;
- a failed or non-array listing;
- more than 16 names, or invalid names;
- an observation over 8192 bytes;
- a report line over 8192 bytes, or a failing report write. Either error replaces the admission rejection, and it has no `cause`.

`evaluateNetworkAdmission(observation)` validates the record's complete shape:
- exact keys and tag;
- 1–16 entries, with valid, strictly ascending names;
- each field is a string or an exact `{unavailable: CODE}`.

It **throws** `Network admission rejected: <fixed reason>` on every rejection. Otherwise it returns a deep-frozen summary. It admits only if all of the following hold:

1. **Loopback.** Exactly one entry is named `lo`. It is a `symlink` whose flags include IFF_UP (0x1) and IFF_LOOPBACK (0x8). Its type is 772 and its operstate is `unknown` or `up`.
2. **Other entries.** Each is one of:
   - a `file` whose three attributes are each `{unavailable: 'ENOTDIR'}`. This exemption applies to kind `file` only.
   - a `symlink` with IFF_UP and IFF_LOOPBACK clear, type not 772, and operstate exactly `down`.
3. **No volatile bits.** No entry has RUNNING (0x40), LOWER_UP (0x10000) or DORMANT (0x20000) set. Sysfs `flags` is expected not to carry these bits, so their presence fails closed.
4. **Addresses.** Exactly one addressed interface, `lo`. It must have `127.0.0.1`/IPv4/internal. `::1`/IPv6/internal is optional. No other address and no duplicates are allowed.

Parsing rules:
- Flags: `^0x(0|[1-9a-f][0-9a-f]{0,7})$`.
- Type: `^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,4})$`, at most 65535.

Any other value, kind, unavailable field or reader error rejects.

## 4. Egress canary

`egressCanaryBlocked(settled)` takes a `Promise.allSettled` result for the canary fetch. It returns true only when the fetch was rejected and `reason.cause.code`, or a direct `reason.code`, is `ENETUNREACH`. Every other outcome fails and bootstrap throws:
- success;
- timeout or abort;
- refusal;
- any other code;
- a missing or malformed outcome.

Scope (lead decision): the IPv4 documentation address `192.0.2.1:8080` only. No grant is added.

Given the interface rule, `ENETUNREACH` at the next real run is consistent with no IPv4 route covering that address. It is **not independent proof**: an ICMP net-unreachable received during SYN_SENT can also produce it. IPv6 routing is not measured.

## Scoped reads and current-fact consistency

The read port exposes only readiness(), loadFacts(lookup, transaction, now) and no generic query, write or list operation. lookup contains the authenticated actorId plus exact organizationId, branchId and capability. The resolver validates these before any persistence access. Each production call requires an explicit caller-owned ClientSession in an active snapshot transaction; no session-less fallback, nested transaction, unrelated session, cache, provider call or automatic retry. Missing/invalid session/readiness denies before authority reads. The adapter never starts/commits/ends the caller's transaction. It projects only required authority fields and returns plain immutable data to rules.

Exact Mongo query restrictions:

1. User: {_id: actorId, userType: 'user', isActive: true}; project ID/type/active only. This is an individual identity lookup, not a private patient/profile fetch.
2. Organization: {_id: organizationId, state: 'active', branches: {$elemMatch: {branchId, state: 'active'}}}; require exactly one matching embedded branch. A legacy business ID is read only after this mapping succeeds.
3. Pharmacy business: {_id: sourceBusinessId, isActive: true, isVerified: true, archivedAt: {$exists: false}}; project only ID/status and fingerprint source fields. Any present archivedAt, even malformed/null, denies under this strict new boundary. Unsupported kind denies before querying another business collection.
4. Membership: {organizationId, actorId, state: 'active', validFrom: {$lte: now}, expiresAt: {$gt: now}, grants: {$elemMatch: {branchId, capability}}}. Enforce one current row and one matching grant; ambiguity denies.
5. Professional eligibility: {organizationId, actorId, profession: requiredProfession, state: 'verified', validFrom: {$lte: now}, expiresAt: {$gt: now}}. Enforce one row and matching branch/capability in the verification decision.
6. Each decision: {_id: referencedDecisionId, organizationId, decisionKind: expectedKind, authorityGeneration: acceptedGeneration}; grant and professional decisions additionally require subjectActorId=actorId. Compare the full binding/digest in rules. Do not merge an externally supplied filter or use $or to relax these predicates.

Authority construction is the explicitly narrow bootstrap query boundary preceding a verified BusinessScope; it may inspect only the requesting person's authority in the exact requested organization. It is not a generic exception allowing other modules to read unscoped business or patient records. No list/count/aggregate/export/file/job surface is added in this slice. Future private business repositories must require the minted scope and compose restrictive ownership/branch predicates on every operation.

Capture one finite server time from an injected trusted clock per resolution, never a request timestamp; pass that exact value to loadFacts and rules. Require validFrom <= now < expiresAt for membership and professional eligibility, with finite dates and valid intervals. Require mapping/grant/verification decisions not in the future. Scope expiresAt is the earlier membership/eligibility expiry. Every invocation reloads facts in its transaction; no JWT role cache or cross-request reuse. Database errors, missing/duplicate rows, malformed facts, unknown evidence and readiness failure reject; no catch returns an allow result.

A successful result is a deeply frozen, internally minted BusinessScope containing actorId, organizationId, exactly one branchId, purpose=staff, capability, kind/sourceBusinessId, organization/branch/membership/eligibility revisions, exact decision/evidence references, checkedAt and expiresAt. Minting uses a module-private runtime identity check (for example, a WeakSet) rather than trusting a caller-shaped object or TypeScript brand alone. Do not include patient details, license contents, bearer tokens or unnecessary profile data. This is a reusable internal authority result, not a new session/JWT or proof of patient consent.

## Actor and owner rule

An ordinary customer is **exact** authenticated `userType === 'user'`. The account owner is the signed `_id`, unchanged. A dependent reference does not confer another account's booking authority.

After existing route validation, both writes must reject absent/null principal, missing/nonstring/whitespace-only `_id`, or missing/nonstring/whitespace-only `userType` with **401 `UNAUTHORIZED` / `Authentication is required`**, before HR readonly dispatch or any BookingService call. Reuse the current read-actor guard's exact validation. Trimming detects blank actor fields only; never rewrite signed IDs or add ObjectId validation to them.

For an exact customer, an omitted validated query `userId` or a value strictly equal to signed `_id` selects signed `_id`. Every other supplied value throws **403 `FORBIDDEN` / `Access to bookings owned by another user is not permitted`**, before service/query/effect dispatch, regardless of whether the booking exists. Do not echo supplied IDs. Query self cannot grant ownership of a foreign resource. No preliminary unscoped read, user existence check, owner retry/fallback or extra prefetch is allowed.

Preserve PUT → `bookingService.update(id, validatedBody, signedOwner)` exactly once, and DELETE → `bookingService.delete(id, signedOwner)` exactly once. The existing service then performs its existing single scoped getById prefetch. An existing foreign booking ID and a missing booking ID both yield **404 `BOOKING_NOT_FOUND` / `Booking not found`**, before downstream write/scheduler/slot/meeting work. This is an initial-read guarantee subject to the race limit below.

For well-shaped other actors, preserve query-owner forwarding and existing behavior. Exact HR still gets **403 `FORBIDDEN` / `HR has view-only access to bookings`**, before service. Unknown nonempty roles and other role paths remain unresolved authority risks; preserving them is not approval. Malformed actors cannot fall through to any preserved branch.

## P0 limits that this ownership contract does not approve

**Own-write field authority remains P0.** Existing update Joi admits `paymentStatus` including `paid`/`refunded`, booking `status` including completed/cancelled, `corporateId`, `slotId`, prescription/report/followUp/documents and other fields. The service derives lifecycle state and can set a cancellation to `refunded`. Caller `lifecycle` is not a directly admitted Joi field, although the service derives lifecycle patches and the internal DTO contains it. Do not invent a new allowlist/denylist, strip fields, or treat own-resource access as authorization to self-assert payment, clinical authorship, corporate affiliation, completion, follow-up benefits or lifecycle transitions. Source and eventual narrow owner checks cannot close these separate actor/field/finance/clinical risks.

**Effects are real implementation paths, not approved business policies.** Update can clear/schedule reminders, activate follow-up benefits, mutate refund-marked state and cancel/sync meetings. Delete clears reminder jobs, can cancel an existing Google Calendar event and update virtualMeeting metadata, can read/decrement a slot count, then hard-deletes the booking. Slot-decrement errors are logged and caught before delete. A meeting/queue/slot error can occur after earlier effects; no transaction/rollback/compensation or refund guarantee is supplied by this slice. A `refunded` field is not evidence of returned money. Successful own deletion, retention/audit, paid cancellation and provider/resource cleanup policy need their separate finance/clinical/privacy decisions. No new deletion/refund rule is invented here.

**Read-then-write race remains P0.** The initial scoped prefetch is followed by ownerless `{_id:id}` mutations and, on applicable paths, ownerless follow-up/meeting writes or effects. This is not an atomic ownership predicate at the final write, a lock, a version check or a transaction. Intervening owner reassignment/replacement or concurrent state changes can invalidate the prefetched snapshot; concurrent delete can also follow earlier effects. Stable ownership in synthetic fixtures is a fixture assumption, not a proven invariant for all production writers. This contract does not claim race-safe authorization and must not be accepted as one. A separate repository/transaction/state contract must establish any stronger invariant before that risk is closed.

# Delegated prescription and recovery policy decisions

12 November 2026. The owner answered the clinical/finance decision question: “you cna decide yourself”. Root accepts responsibility for selecting product and technical policy. These are the selected development defaults; exact implementation contracts and independent reviews still precede code. This delegation does not make an AI a pharmacist, verify a professional, approve a real prescription, deploy code or authorize real money/stock actions. Qualified human decisions on individual cases remain part of the implemented workflow.

## Selected operating policy

| Boundary | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Reviewer identity | Use an individual authenticated person, not a shared pharmacy business login. Require current active account, explicit current business/branch review capability and independently verified professional eligibility. OTP verification, customer linkage, business verification and administrator status alone confer no clinical-review authority. |
| Grant/verification authority | Separate membership/capability grants, credential verification and clinical review. No user may verify themselves or gain authority through a profile field. Existing self-editable Admin.permissions is not a trusted capability registry. Provision protected grants through separately reviewed authority/bootstrap controls; absent grants fail closed. |
| Clinical decision | A verified authorized pharmacist approves/rejects the actual prescription. The application and AI do not decide medical validity. Require protected reviewer identity/time/reason/evidence references; bind the decision to immutable document, patient and order-item versions. Reject mismatched, stale, revoked or unknown evidence. Attachment alone never approves dispensing. |
| Progress | Block packed, ready-for-pickup, dispatch and completion unless the required current review is eligible. Keep payment requirements separate. A new order may remain awaiting review, with truthful customer status and a controlled cancellation path; never auto-approve or relabel it not_required to unblock it. |
| Patient/payer | Keep the clinical patient distinct from login, payer, pharmacy customer link and dependent-account ownership. No phone/name merge or assumed guardian consent. Verification and purpose-bound representation are explicit dependencies of clinical enablement. |
| Before handover | Cancellation must establish controlled custody/no handover, claim the transition once, release only the exact live reservation and durably create any money-return obligation. A stock release is not a financial refund. |
| After dispatch/handover | Use a separate return/failed-delivery/exception workflow. Do not put physically dispatched or returned goods directly into saleable stock. Inspection/quality disposition and financial settlement are separate recorded decisions. |
| Legacy ready/out orders | Keep an accountable recovery case/worklist. Reconcile actual custody, reservation and payment facts per order. No blanket completion, database backfill, deletion, forced cancellation or assumed refund. Unknown facts remain blocked for an authorized operator. |
| Funds proof | Treat authorization, capture, settlement, wallet debit, cash collection and refund as distinct facts. The existing paid/refunded labels are not sufficient proof. Bind server-side resource, payer, amount, currency and provider references; ignore client-selected fulfillment context. |
| Refund destination | Return each verified funded component to its original instrument by default. Do not silently replace a gateway refund with application wallet credit. An alternate destination requires a separately recorded, explicit customer choice and verified authority. |
| Amount/budget | Use explicit currency and integer minor units in new intents, with reviewed conversions at legacy rupee boundaries. Reserve outstanding refund budget transactionally against verified capture/debit facts. No rounding, omitted amount, duplicate payout or provider-fee deduction is used to repair uncertain records. |
| Completion/retry | Persist one operation identity and payload hash before effects. Mark refunded only after a matching confirmed financial effect. Pending, failed and unknown are not completed. Reconcile ambiguous provider outcomes; do not generate a new operation key or blindly repeat an unproved effect. |
| Financial/operations roles | Explicit current finance/recovery and pharmacy-operations capabilities authorize their own decisions. Clinical approval does not grant refund authority, and financial authority does not approve a prescription or stock quality. All privileged decisions use protected audit references. |

Existing source requires repair before it can implement this policy: no individual pharmacist membership/credential system exists; authorized gateway payments are currently accepted as paid; pharmacy timeout recovery credits an application wallet instead of a gateway refund; duplicate ledger errors can be mistaken for completed refunds. See [the source baseline](PHARMACY_AUTHORITY_RECOVERY_BASELINE.md). Do not reuse these labels or helpers as trusted proof without their separate hardening contracts.

## Provider facts checked for the policy

Razorpay's payment fetch schema distinguishes authorized/captured states and exposes captured flag, order reference, currency, payment amount and refunded amount in currency subunits. A local paid flag or a valid callback signature alone does not establish the selected application's capture invariant. [Payment API](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/payments/fetch-with-id/), [integration capture guidance](https://razorpay.com/docs/server-integration/python/test-app/).

The Normal Refund API requires eligible captured funds, positive integer subunits and supported payment methods; an omitted amount can request the full refund. Its receipt detects reuse on the same payment. Our adapter must reconcile the existing operation on duplicates/uncertain responses, not assume a universal idempotency header. Exact endpoint/SDK behavior must be frozen before implementation. [Normal Refund API](https://razorpay.com/docs/api/refunds/create-normal/).

## Implementation sequence and retained gates

1. Contract the existing false-paid/false-refunded and privilege-write hazards before using them as authority.
2. Freeze shared person, business membership/capability, professional verification and protected decision interfaces; reuse them across pharmacy and lab roles rather than duplicate identity systems.
3. Implement version-bound prescription review/revocation and guarded progress with separately scoped staff authority.
4. Implement durable cancellation/recovery/refund coordination, exact reservation effects, provider reconciliation and honest client-facing states. Preserve legacy records until a reviewed recovery decision exists.
5. Obtain focused success/denial, index/transaction, replay/race/crash and source-composition evidence under C3. Root dependency/runtime/start adoption still retains C2. Final cross-module integration campaign remains DEFERRED_BY_OWNER.

F1 stays HIGH/open until approval and legacy recovery paths actually exist and the required evidence is accepted. The earlier progress gate only mitigates entry into the dead end. Real clinical/financial/operator provisioning and release approvals remain explicit; no names or credentials are fabricated. We will not stop technical development for another product-policy confirmation, but new policies do not authorize live effects or waive application/security gates. Corporate/HR/hospital expansion remains deferred.

## Rows, aggregate and exact projection

One row is one stored embedded batch occurrence with exact selected status. Count batch occurrences, not inventory items, medicines or units. Include inactive items and zero-quantity holds; deactivation/quantity cannot hide a recall. Active/depleted/unknown statuses and absent/empty/non-array batches contribute no rows. Do not synthesize batches from aggregate counters.

Use one aggregate:

1. First match mandatory pharmacyId as the validated own ObjectId plus an embedded selected-status prefilter and explicit $expr:{$isArray:'$batches'} before unwind. Absent/null/scalar-object batches are excluded; Mongo unwind treating a scalar as one element must never create a worklist row. No caller criteria spread or optional scope.
2. Project only required item/batch source fields, unwind actual batches with includeArrayIndex=batchPosition, and match the selected stored status AGAIN. An item prefilter alone would include its active sibling batches.
3. One facet from this same filtered stream: metadata count BEFORE pagination/catalogue join; data sorted item _id ascending then batchPosition ascending, skipped by (page-1)*limit, limited to limit. Never paginate items before unwind, sum quantities, or load the complete list into application memory.
4. After the page bound, at most one global medicines _id lookup per row may supply name only through an explicit projection. Preserve rows/count when the catalogue reference is missing; no destructive unwind or private business/patient join.

def require(ok, message):
    if not ok:
        raise RuntimeError(message)


def closed(value, keys):
    return type(value) is dict and set(value) == set(keys)


def exact(value, expected):
    if type(value) is not type(expected):
        return False
    if type(value) is dict:
        return set(value) == set(expected) and all(exact(value[k], expected[k]) for k in value)
    if type(value) is list:
        return len(value) == len(expected) and all(exact(v, e) for v, e in zip(value, expected))
    return value == expected


def digest(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def load(data):
    # Duplicate keys and non-JSON numbers cannot hide a contradictory receipt.
    def pairs(rows):
        result = {}
        for key, value in rows:
            require(key not in result, 'Duplicate JSON key')
            result[key] = value
        return result
    return json.loads(data, object_pairs_hook=pairs,
                      parse_constant=lambda value: require(False, 'Nonfinite JSON number'))


def ident(path):
    s = path.lstat()
    return (s.st_dev, s.st_ino, s.st_uid, s.st_gid, s.st_mode,
            0 if stat.S_ISDIR(s.st_mode) else s.st_nlink)


def read_regular(path, expected=None, private=False):
    path = pathlib.Path(path)
    before = path.lstat()
    require(stat.S_ISREG(before.st_mode) and before.st_nlink == 1, 'Regular single-link input required: ' + str(path))
    if private:
        require(before.st_uid == 501 and stat.S_IMODE(before.st_mode) == 0o600, 'Private Root receipt required')
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    try:
        opened = os.fstat(fd)
        require((before.st_dev, before.st_ino) == (opened.st_dev, opened.st_ino), 'Input replaced during open')
        chunks = []
        while block := os.read(fd, 65536):
            chunks.append(block)
        data = b''.join(chunks)
        after = os.fstat(fd)
        require((opened.st_size, opened.st_mtime_ns, opened.st_ctime_ns) ==
                (after.st_size, after.st_mtime_ns, after.st_ctime_ns) and ident(path) ==
                (opened.st_dev, opened.st_ino, opened.st_uid, opened.st_gid, opened.st_mode, opened.st_nlink), 'Input changed during read')
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
    if expected is not None:
        actual = {'sha256': digest(data), 'bytes': len(data), 'kind': 'regular',
                  'uid': before.st_uid, 'gid': before.st_gid, 'mode': oct(stat.S_IMODE(before.st_mode)), 'nlink': before.st_nlink}
        require(actual == expected, 'Pinned input changed: ' + str(path))
    return data


def write_new(path, data):
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
    try:
        require(os.write(fd, data) == len(data), 'Incomplete exclusive file write')
        os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
    return ident(path)


def encoded(value):
    return (json.dumps(value, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + '\n').encode()


def validate_receipt():
    require(sys.argv == [str(OPERATOR)] and pathlib.Path(sys.executable).resolve() == pathlib.Path(PYTHON), 'Fixed Python invocation only')
    require(sys.flags.isolated and sys.flags.no_site and sys.dont_write_bytecode, 'Use env -i pinned Python -I -S -B')
    require(dict(os.environ) == {'__CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING': '0x1F5:0x0:0x0', 'LC_CTYPE': 'C.UTF-8'}, 'Unexpected Python startup environment')
    os.environ.clear()
    require(not os.environ, 'Empty parent environment required')
    raw = read_regular(APPROVAL, private=True)
    approval = load(raw)
    require(closed(approval, ['schema', 'scope', 'issuer', 'operatorAuthor', 'sourceAuthor', 'cwd', 'branch', 'approvedHead',
                             'operatorSha256', 'manifestSha256', 'sourceFreezeSha256', 'offlineResultSha256', 'votes']), 'Closed receipt schema required')
    require(approval['schema'] == 'SD-AUTHORITY-REAL-APPROVAL-1' and approval['scope'] == SCOPE and approval['issuer'] == '/root'
            and approval['operatorAuthor'] == AUTHOR and approval['sourceAuthor'] == '/root/claude_review_5_packet'
            and approval['cwd'] == str(ROOT) and approval['branch'] == 'm0/authority-pure-runtime'
            and re.fullmatch(r'[a-f0-9]{40}', approval['approvedHead']), 'Receipt fixed binding rejected')
    for key in ['operatorSha256', 'manifestSha256', 'sourceFreezeSha256', 'offlineResultSha256']:
        require(type(approval[key]) is str and re.fullmatch(HEX, approval[key]), 'Receipt hash malformed')
    require(digest(read_regular(OPERATOR)) == approval['operatorSha256'], 'Operator hash not approved')
    manifest_raw = read_regular(MANIFEST)
    require(digest(manifest_raw) == approval['manifestSha256'], 'Manifest hash not approved')
    manifest = load(manifest_raw)
    require(approval['sourceFreezeSha256'] == manifest['sourceFreezeSha256'] == '7df6a0ba88c5cf1e19cb79fdbcfe3cf1e4ec67175d6f4b0102b817c868d554dc'
            and approval['offlineResultSha256'] == manifest['offlineResultSha256'] == 'dfa34ddafc26100da6a82c07a0e48a1010d202e5d8c188cd49831d20a8e112cc', 'Source/offline binding rejected')
    require(type(approval['votes']) is list and len(approval['votes']) == 2, 'Two actual votes required')
    reviewers = set()
    for vote in approval['votes']:
        require(closed(vote, ['reviewer', 'role', 'decision', 'scope', 'approvedHead', 'operatorSha256', 'manifestSha256',
                             'sourceFreezeSha256', 'offlineResultSha256', 'findings']), 'Closed vote schema required')
        require(type(vote['reviewer']) is str and re.fullmatch(r'/root(?:/[a-z0-9_]+)*', vote['reviewer'])
                and vote['reviewer'] not in [AUTHOR, approval['sourceAuthor']] and vote['reviewer'] not in reviewers,
                'Distinct actual nonauthors required')
        reviewers.add(vote['reviewer'])
        require(vote['decision'] == 'APPROVE_SOURCE_AND_ONE_FIXED_AUTHORITY_PURE_RUN' and vote['findings'] == [], 'Unconditional exact vote required')
        for key in ['scope', 'approvedHead', 'operatorSha256', 'manifestSha256', 'sourceFreezeSha256', 'offlineResultSha256']:
            require(vote[key] == approval[key], 'Vote does not bind this exact candidate')
    require({v['role'] for v in approval['votes']} == {'Standards', 'Spec'}, 'Standards and Spec required')
    return approval, raw, manifest


class Capture:
    """Only the fixed sequence below calls this bounded stream recorder."""
    def __init__(self, approval, approval_raw, manifest):
        self.approval, self.approval_raw, self.manifest = approval, approval_raw, manifest
        self.area = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='sd-authority-real-', dir='/private/tmp'))
        os.chmod(self.area, 0o700)
        self.area_id = ident(self.area)
        self.files = {}
        self.marker = encoded({'runId': str(uuid.uuid4()), 'approvedHead': approval['approvedHead']})
        self.new('.operator-owner.json', self.marker)
        self.config = self.area / 'docker'
        self.config.mkdir(mode=0o700)
        self.config_id = ident(self.config)
        self.config_bytes = b'{"auths":{}}\n'
        self.config_file_id = write_new(self.config / 'config.json', self.config_bytes)
        self.report = {'status': 'IN_PROGRESS', 'approvedHead': approval['approvedHead'], 'operatorSha256': approval['operatorSha256'],
                       'manifestSha256': approval['manifestSha256'], 'areaRetained': str(self.area), 'launcherInvocations': 0,
                       'overallClaimConsumed': False, 'commands': [], 'firstProblem': None, 'secondaryProblems': [],
                       'cleanupErrors': [], 'processCleanupUnresolved': False, 'resources': None, 'postchecks': {}, 'resultWritten': False}
        self.new('result.json', encoded(self.report))

    def new(self, name, data):
        require(ident(self.area) == self.area_id, 'Capture area lost before allocation')
        self.files[name] = write_new(self.area / name, data)

    def owned(self):
        require(ident(self.area) == self.area_id and ident(self.config) == self.config_id, 'Capture/config directory ownership lost')
        require(ident(self.area / '.operator-owner.json') == self.files['.operator-owner.json']
                and read_regular(self.area / '.operator-owner.json', private=True) == self.marker, 'Capture marker changed')
        require(ident(self.config / 'config.json') == self.config_file_id
                and read_regular(self.config / 'config.json', private=True) == self.config_bytes, 'Blank config changed')

    def save(self):
        self.owned()
        path = self.area / 'result.json'
        require(ident(path) == self.files['result.json'], 'Result identity lost')
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
        try:
            require(tuple([os.fstat(fd).st_dev, os.fstat(fd).st_ino]) == self.files['result.json'][:2], 'Result replaced during open')
            data = encoded(self.report)
            os.ftruncate(fd, 0)
            require(os.write(fd, data) == len(data), 'Result write incomplete')
            os.fsync(fd)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)

    def freeze(self):
        self.owned()
        require(read_regular(APPROVAL, private=True) == self.approval_raw, 'Private receipt changed')
        require(digest(read_regular(OPERATOR)) == self.approval['operatorSha256']
                and digest(read_regular(MANIFEST)) == self.approval['manifestSha256'], 'Operator/manifest drift')
        for name, expected in self.manifest['files'].items():
            read_regular(ROOT / name, expected)
        for path, expected in self.manifest['tools'].items():
            read_regular(path, expected)
        require(ident(ALIAS) == tuple(self.manifest['dockerAlias']['identity']) and ALIAS.is_symlink()
                and os.readlink(ALIAS) == DOCKER and ALIAS.lstat().st_uid == 0, 'Docker alias drift')
        require(ident(SOCKET) == tuple(self.manifest['socket']['identity']) and stat.S_ISSOCK(SOCKET.lstat().st_mode), 'Socket identity drift')

    def command(self, label, argv, env, cwd, seconds=20, caps=None, nonzero_ok=False, launcher=False):
        # Early attempted row survives capture allocation, Popen and every finalization failure.
        caps = {'stdout': 8192, 'stderr': 8192} if caps is None else caps
        row = {'label': label, 'argv': argv, 'env': env, 'cwd': str(cwd), 'attempted': True, 'processStarted': False,
               'pid': None, 'returnCode': None, 'executionLimitSeconds': seconds, 'cleanupLimitSeconds': 5,
               'firstProblem': None, 'secondaryProblems': [], 'cleanupErrors': [], 'unresolved': False, 'unresolvedReasons': [], 'terminationRefused': False, 'captures': {
                   stream: {'path': str(self.area / (label + '.' + stream)), 'allocated': False, 'identity': None,
                            'observedBytesAtLeast': 0, 'retainedBytes': 0, 'limit': cap, 'eof': False, 'complete': False,
                            'ownershipVerified': False, 'sha256': None} for stream, cap in caps.items()}}
        self.report['commands'].append(row)
        proc = selector = None
        handles = {}
        cleanup_deadline = None
        killed = False
        stderr_pending = bytearray()
        def problem(code, exc=None):
            value = {'code': code, 'type': None if exc is None else type(exc).__name__, 'message': None if exc is None else str(exc)[:2048]}
            if row['firstProblem'] is None:
                row['firstProblem'] = value
            else:
                row['secondaryProblems'].append(value)
        def unresolved(code, exc=None):
            # Cleanup uncertainty never replaces the original timeout/overflow/error.
            row['unresolved'] = True
            self.report['processCleanupUnresolved'] = True
            if code not in row['unresolvedReasons']:
                row['unresolvedReasons'].append(code)
                row['cleanupErrors'].append({'code': code, 'type': None if exc is None else type(exc).__name__,
                                             'message': None if exc is None else str(exc)[:2048]})
            if row['firstProblem'] is None:
                problem(code, exc)
            if self.report['firstProblem'] is None:
                self.report['firstProblem'] = row['firstProblem']
        def terminate():
            nonlocal killed
            if proc is None or killed or row['terminationRefused']:
                return
            try:
                if proc.poll() is not None:
                    if any(not c['eof'] for c in row['captures'].values()):
                        # The exited leader cannot prove ownership of pipe holders.
                        # Do not signal a stale/reused group or infer their absence.
                        unresolved('EXITED_LEADER_OPEN_PIPES_UNRESOLVED')
                    return
                require(os.getpgid(proc.pid) == proc.pid, 'Owned new process group lost')
                os.killpg(proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                killed = True
            except BaseException as exc:
                row['terminationRefused'] = True
                unresolved('PROCESS_GROUP_OWNERSHIP_OR_TERMINATION_UNKNOWN', exc)
                raise
        try:
            self.save()
            self.owned()
            for stream, capture in row['captures'].items():
                name = label + '.' + stream
                self.new(name, b'')
                capture['allocated'] = True
                capture['identity'] = self.files[name]
                fd = os.open(self.area / name, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
                handles[stream] = fd
                require(ident(self.area / name) == self.files[name] and (os.fstat(fd).st_dev, os.fstat(fd).st_ino) == self.files[name][:2], 'Capture replaced before open')
            self.save()
            if launcher:
                # All preparation is complete; consuming before the sole Node host Popen is deliberate.
                require(self.report['launcherInvocations'] == 0, 'Launcher already attempted')
                self.report['launcherInvocations'] = 1
                self.save()
            proc = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                    stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, start_new_session=True)
            row['processStarted'] = True
            row['pid'] = proc.pid
            self.save()
            selector = selectors.DefaultSelector()
            selector.register(proc.stdout, selectors.EVENT_READ, 'stdout')
            selector.register(proc.stderr, selectors.EVENT_READ, 'stderr')
            deadline = time.monotonic() + seconds
            while selector.get_map():
                if row['firstProblem'] is None and time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                    problem('EXECUTION_TIMEOUT')
                if row['firstProblem'] is not None and cleanup_deadline is None:
                    cleanup_deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
                if cleanup_deadline is not None:
                    terminate()
                    if time.monotonic() >= cleanup_deadline:
                        unresolved('PIPE_DRAIN_DEADLINE_UNRESOLVED')
                        raise RuntimeError('Finite pipe cleanup expired')
                for key, _ in selector.select(0.05):
                    block = os.read(key.fd, 4096)
                    capture = row['captures'][key.data]
                    if not block:
                        capture['eof'] = True
                        selector.unregister(key.fileobj)
                        key.fileobj.close()
                        continue
                    capture['observedBytesAtLeast'] += len(block)
                    prefix = block[:max(0, capture['limit'] - capture['retainedBytes'])]
                    if capture['observedBytesAtLeast'] > capture['limit']:
                        problem(key.data.upper() + '_OVERFLOW') if row['firstProblem'] is None else None
                    if prefix:
                        self.owned()
                        name = label + '.' + key.data
                        require(ident(self.area / name) == self.files[name], 'Capture ownership changed before write')
                        n = os.write(handles[key.data], prefix)
                        capture['retainedBytes'] += n
                        require(n == len(prefix), 'Capture write incomplete')
                        if launcher and key.data == 'stderr':
                            stderr_pending.extend(prefix)
                            while b'\n' in stderr_pending:
                                line, _, rest = stderr_pending.partition(b'\n')
                                stderr_pending[:] = rest
                                try:
                                    early = load(line)
                                except (ValueError, RuntimeError):
                                    continue
                                if type(early) is dict and early.get('phase') == 'created':
                                    resource = resource_identity(line.decode('utf-8', errors='strict'))
                                    if self.report['resources'] is not None:
                                        self.report['resourceIdentityUnresolved'] = True
                                    require(self.report['resources'] is None, 'Contradictory/duplicate early identity')
                                    self.report['resources'] = resource
                                    self.save()
            # A child may close pipes before exiting. It still gets only its original execution deadline.
            if cleanup_deadline is None:
                try:
                    row['returnCode'] = proc.wait(timeout=max(0, deadline - time.monotonic()))
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    problem('EXECUTION_TIMEOUT')
                    cleanup_deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
                    terminate()
            if row['returnCode'] is None:
                row['returnCode'] = proc.wait(timeout=max(0, cleanup_deadline - time.monotonic()))
            if row['returnCode'] != 0 and not nonzero_ok:
                problem('COMMAND_NONZERO_EXIT')
        except BaseException as exc:
            problem('COMMAND_EXCEPTION', exc)
        finally:
            if cleanup_deadline is None:
                cleanup_deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
            if proc is not None:
                try:
                    terminate()
                    row['returnCode'] = proc.wait(timeout=max(0, cleanup_deadline - time.monotonic()))
                except BaseException as exc:
                    unresolved('PROCESS_CLEANUP_FAILED', exc)
                if any(not c['eof'] for c in row['captures'].values()):
                    unresolved('PIPE_EOF_UNRESOLVED_AT_FINALIZATION')
                for pipe in [proc.stdout, proc.stderr]:
                    try:
                        pipe.close()
                    except BaseException as exc:
                        unresolved('PIPE_CLOSE_FAILED', exc)
            if selector is not None:
                try:
                    selector.close()
                except BaseException as exc:
                    unresolved('SELECTOR_CLOSE_FAILED', exc)
            for fd in handles.values():
                try:
                    os.close(fd)
                except BaseException as exc:
                    unresolved('CAPTURE_CLOSE_FAILED', exc)
            try:
                self.owned()
                for stream, capture in row['captures'].items():
                    if not capture['allocated']:
                        continue
                    name = label + '.' + stream
                    require(ident(self.area / name) == self.files[name], 'Capture identity lost; refusing read')
                    data = read_regular(self.area / name, private=True)
                    require(len(data) == capture['retainedBytes'] <= capture['limit'], 'Capture size changed')
                    capture['ownershipVerified'] = True
                    capture['sha256'] = digest(data)
                    capture['complete'] = capture['eof'] and capture['observedBytesAtLeast'] == len(data) and row['firstProblem'] is None and not row['cleanupErrors']
                self.save()
            except BaseException as exc:
                unresolved('OWNERSHIP_OR_FINALIZATION_UNRESOLVED', exc)
        return row

    def text(self, row, stream, partial=False):
        self.owned()
        capture = row['captures'][stream]
        require(capture['ownershipVerified'] and ident(pathlib.Path(capture['path'])) == tuple(capture['identity']), 'Unsafe capture read denied')
        data = read_regular(capture['path'], private=True)
        require(digest(data) == capture['sha256'], 'Capture changed after finalization')
        return data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace' if partial else 'strict')

    def complete(self, row):
        require(not row['unresolved'] and row['firstProblem'] is None and not row['cleanupErrors'] and all(c['complete'] for c in row['captures'].values()), 'Command evidence incomplete: ' + row['label'])

    def git_clean(self, phase):
        fixed = [([GIT, 'rev-parse', '--verify', 'HEAD'], self.approval['approvedHead'] + '\n'),
                 ([GIT, 'symbolic-ref', '--short', 'HEAD'], 'm0/authority-pure-runtime\n'),
                 ([GIT, '--no-optional-locks', '-c', 'core.fsmonitor=false', '-c', 'core.untrackedCache=false',
                   'status', '--porcelain=v1', '--untracked-files=all', '--ignore-submodules=none'], '')]
        for index, (argv, expected) in enumerate(fixed):
            row = self.command(phase + '-git-' + str(index), argv, GIT_ENV, ROOT)
            self.complete(row)
            require(self.text(row, 'stdout') == expected, 'Exact clean committed candidate required')

    def docker(self, label, args, nonzero_ok=False):
        self.freeze()
        return self.command(label, [DOCKER, '--config', str(self.config), '--host', ENDPOINT] + args,
                            {'PATH': '/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin'}, self.area, nonzero_ok=nonzero_ok)

    def engine(self, label):
        row = self.docker(label, INFO)
        self.complete(row)
        require(load(self.text(row, 'stdout')) == [ENGINE, 'linux'], 'Same approved Linux engine required')

    def labels(self, label):
        row = self.docker(label, LABELS)
        self.complete(row)
        require(self.text(row, 'stdout').strip() == '', 'Existing purpose labels; no adoption or mutation')


def resource_identity(stderr):
    rows = []
    for line in stderr.splitlines():
        try:
            value = load(line)
        except (ValueError, RuntimeError):
            continue
        if type(value) is dict and value.get('phase') == 'created':
            require(closed(value, ['phase', 'id', 'runId', 'directory']) and re.fullmatch(HEX, value['id'])
                    and re.fullmatch(UUID, value['runId']) and re.fullmatch(r'/private/tmp/sd-app-isolation-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{6,32}', value['directory']), 'Malformed early created identity')
            rows.append(value)
    require(len(rows) == 1, 'Missing or contradictory early created identity; unresolved resource')
    return rows[0]


def network_proof(value):
    require(closed(value, ['tag', 'observation', 'loopback', 'controlFiles', 'downDevices', 'loopbackAddresses'])
            and value['tag'] == 'APP-NET-ADMIT-1' and value['loopback'] == 'lo', 'Network summary schema')
    observation = value['observation']
    require(closed(observation, ['tag', 'entries', 'addressedInterfaces']) and observation['tag'] == 'APP-NET-DIAG-1', 'Network observation schema')
    entries = observation['entries']
    require(type(entries) is list and 1 <= len(entries) <= 16, 'Network entries bounds')
    names = []
    controls, down = [], []
    for entry in entries:
        require(closed(entry, ['name', 'kind', 'flags', 'operstate', 'type']) and type(entry['name']) is str
                and re.fullmatch(r'(?!\.{1,2}$)[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,32}', entry['name']), 'Network entry schema')
        name = entry['name']
        names.append(name)
        if name != 'lo' and entry['kind'] == 'file':
            require(all(entry[f] == {'unavailable': 'ENOTDIR'} for f in ['flags', 'operstate', 'type']), 'Control file state')
            controls.append(name)
            continue
        require(entry['kind'] == 'symlink' and type(entry['flags']) is str and re.fullmatch(r'0x(0|[1-9a-f][0-9a-f]{0,7})', entry['flags'])
                and type(entry['type']) is str and re.fullmatch(r'(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,4})', entry['type']) and int(entry['type']) <= 65535, 'Device state malformed')
        flags = int(entry['flags'], 16)
        if name == 'lo':
            require(flags & 9 == 9 and flags & 0x30040 == 0 and entry['type'] == '772'
                    and entry['operstate'] in ['up', 'unknown'], 'Loopback state rejected')
        else:
            require(flags & 0x30049 == 0 and entry['type'] != '772' and entry['operstate'] == 'down', 'Nonloopback state rejected')
            down.append(name)
    require(names == sorted(set(names)) and names.count('lo') == 1, 'Network names/order rejected')
    addressed = observation['addressedInterfaces']
    require(type(addressed) is list and len(addressed) == 1 and closed(addressed[0], ['name', 'addresses']) and addressed[0]['name'] == 'lo', 'Addressed interfaces rejected')
    addresses = addressed[0]['addresses']
    require(type(addresses) is list and 1 <= len(addresses) <= 4, 'Address bounds')
    for row in addresses:
        require(closed(row, ['address', 'family', 'internal']) and row['address'] in ['127.0.0.1', '::1']

## 4. Milestone 2 — pharmacy prescription state at completion

**Disposition: APPROVE_SOURCE_ONLY (contract-conformant); F1 needs an owner decision.**

Confirmed in source (`pharmacyOrders/services/index.ts`):
- The guard (1022–1032) applies only to completion. It is a closed allowlist (`approved` | `not_required`) built from two strict inequalities, so undefined, null, '', pending, rejected and unknown values all get a fixed 409 `ORDER_PRESCRIPTION_APPROVAL_REQUIRED` with no value echoed.
  - It runs after: not found (985), store 403 (988), terminal (991), transition (995–1001), and both payment checks (1003–1020).
  - It runs before: `buildInventoryItems` (1034), the transaction (1039), any order write, release/consume, and the post-commit queues.
  - So unpaid+pending still gets the payment 409.
- CAS filter (1040–1050) is `{_id, status: observed}`, plus `prescriptionStatus: <observed exact value>` only when completing. The predicate is in the filter, not the update body. The update body and `{new:true, session}` are unchanged. For non-completion targets the filter is equivalent to the old `{_id, status}`.
- A CAS miss throws 500 `UPDATE_FAILED` (1052–1054) inside the callback, before release (1056–1058) and consume (1060–1062). Because the predicate binds the observed value, a transient `withTransaction` retry re-runs against the same captured `order` and cannot match a state that has since changed.
- `BaseRepository.findById` is `.lean()` (BaseRepository 41–47), which does not apply schema defaults. A stored document without `prescriptionStatus` therefore reads as undefined and fails closed, as the contract requires. A `PharmacyOrderRepository.findById` override is not visible (repository excerpt is lines 1–35 only).
- The candidate diff touches only these two hunks. The consume helper (220–234), inventory leaf (inventory service 430–451, repository 227–260), controller and routes are unchanged.

**F1 — introduced consequence: unrecoverable non-terminal orders (severity HIGH, operational; owner/clinical decision; not a conformance defect).**
- Scenario:
  - Every order with a prescription-required medicine is created with `pending` (462–478, called at 575). Repricing only re-derives pending/not_required (911).
  - The contract's whole-src1 scan found no first-party command that sets `approved`.
  - The packed, ready and out-for-delivery transitions remain ungated for prescription state (1003–1013). The order can therefore be accepted, packed and moved to `ready_for_pickup` or `out_for_delivery`.
  - From those states `ALLOWED_STATUS_TRANSITIONS` allows only `completed` (30–31). The new guard denies it, and cancel (controller 84–91 → `updateStatus('cancelled')`) fails the transition check with 409.
- Consequence:
  - The order is permanently non-terminal and has no exit in the product.
  - Reserved batch stock is never consumed or released.
  - Payment stays captured.
  - The goods may already have been handed over or dispatched.
  - Scope: every prescription order on the app and in-store counter paths, plus any legacy document missing the field. Before this change the same order completed: clinically unsafe, but recoverable.
- Minimum fix (requires a decision; I am not choosing a policy): any one of:
  - (a) amend the contract so the same closed gate also applies to transitions into `ready_for_pickup`/`out_for_delivery`, or into `packed`, while cancellation is still allowed;
  - (b) deliver the separately contracted pharmacist approval/rejection command before prescription orders are enabled;
  - (c) explicitly accept and record the dead end, with a reviewed recovery procedure.
  Until then, treat F1 as a release blocker for prescription dispensing. Given the owner's recorded pre-launch status, no live impact is asserted.
- **L-P1** — A CAS miss (for example a concurrent revocation) surfaces as a generic 500 `UPDATE_FAILED` and is logged as a server error. The contract accepted this; triage and monitoring should not treat it as an infrastructure fault.

Known risks still open:
- Stored `approved` is not pharmacist authorization or versioned clinical evidence.
- There is no approval command and no provenance.
- Replacing prescription URLs keeps `approved` (925–935). ABA changes and catalogue `prescriptionRequired` defaults are also open.
- Consume uses the pre-transaction snapshot `order.items` (1061), not `nextOrder.items`. The CAS does not bind items, allocations or a version, so correctness relies on `update()` gating item edits by status; that code is not in the packet.
- Packed/release safeguards are open.
- Edit-time available-stock debits on legacy orders (176–194, 937–960) are open.
- Paid cancellation/refund is open.
- The UTC expiry comparison in `consumeBatchAllocations` (inventory repository 237–247) can fail completion with `BATCH_RESERVATION_CONSUME_FAILED` for a lot that expired after reservation. That is another pre-existing stuck path at ready/out.

  - a missing required ID, status or position (L430) gives 503;
